# H6, controlled: asking HR on vague JDs (generated by `python -m app.eval.clarify`; do not edit by hand)

Every NLP501-bench v1 JD (18) gets a vague twin: tool names → their category, year counts → "several years"; the original labels stay (they encode the hiring intent). Ranked by the agent's deterministic scorer (8 rule criteria ⊕ CE, hybrid JD parser). The HR answer is scripted from the original requirements: this tests the mechanism (detect → ask → integrate), not a real HR conversation.

**L1 decision:** the agent asks HR on 15/18 vague twins and on 4/18 original JDs (3 of which are vague by design).

| Condition | nDCG@10 (mean) | Kendall τ (mean) |
|---|---|---|
| clear JD (upper bound) | 0.851 | 0.513 |
| vague twin, nobody asks | 0.626 | 0.451 |
| vague twin, HR asked and answered | 0.756 | 0.507 |
| **the agent as it runs** (HR's answer only where the gate asked) | 0.704 | 0.495 |

Where the gate did not ask (3 twins), the twin still contained a test-type phrase such as "API testing" that the rule counts as a concrete tool, so the rule did not fire and the LLM gate chose to proceed. Asking can also lower a score: the original requirements are stricter than the vague ones.

Asked vs not asked, paired over 18 JDs: ΔnDCG@10 +0.129 (p = 0.000), Δτ +0.056 (p = 0.012). Share of the vague loss recovered: 57%.
